blocks.text: ODED, “A PROPHET OF THE LORD” IN SAMARIA · TWO KINGDOMS
Oded. He met Israel's army at Samaria and told them to send their captives home.
SCRIPTURE CALLS
Prophet
ERA
Two kingdoms 930–586 BC
IN THE DAYS OF
Pekah · Ahaz
BOOK
None bears the name
HOW THE WORD CAME
“But a prophet of the LORD was there, whose name was Oded: and he went out before the host”.
THE CALL
How the word came
“But a prophet of the LORD was there, whose name was Oded: and he went out before the host”. 2 Chronicles 28:9
BEFORE THE KINGS
Before two kings
KING OF ISRAEL
Pekah
“Now hear me therefore, and deliver the captives again, which ye have taken captive of your brethren: for the fierce wrath of the LORD is upon you.”
2 Chronicles 28:11 (KJV) →
KING OF JUDAH
Ahaz
THE MESSAGE
The word in its main themes
A rage that reaches to heaven
“ye have slain them in a rage that reacheth up unto heaven.”
2 Chronicles 28:9 (KJV) →
Your own sins
“but are there not with you, even with you, sins against the LORD your God?”
2 Chronicles 28:10 (KJV) →
Send them back
THE WORD TO …
To whom the word was spoken
TO ISRAEL'S RETURNING ARMY, AT SAMARIA
“deliver the captives again, which ye have taken captive of your brethren”
2 Chronicles 28:11 (KJV) →
COMPANIONS AND OPPONENTS
Who stood with him, and against him
Azariah, Berechiah, Jehizkiah and Amasa, heads of Ephraim
HOW THE STORY ENDS
Scripture says, tradition says
SCRIPTURE SAYS
From the textScripture names Oded only here. 2 Chronicles 28:9
TRADITION SAYS
No tradition is recorded here.
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 1
2 Chronicles 28
PASSAGES · 1
2 Chronicles 28:5–15
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Kings does not tell this episode; it is in Chronicles only.
Chronicles does not say Oded spoke to Pekah himself; he spoke to the army.
He is a different man from Oded the father of Azariah (2 Chronicles 15:1).
